newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Selling maintains pressure on Zimbabwe shares.
newsitem.headline: Selling maintains pressure on Zimbabwe shares.

text.p: Sustained selling by small investors maintained pressure on Zimbabwe's stocks on Monday but analysts say impending corporate results may soon arrest the decline.

The 59-share industrial index dropped 46.99 points or 0.46 percent to close at 10,256.25 -- its 10th straight loss -- downed by declines in retailers Edgars (minus 10 cents) and Tedco (off 25 cents), to 240 and 275 cents respectively.
Wider losses were seen in agro-industrialists Chemco which dropped 500 cents to 4,500 and bankers Barclays which lost 60 to 3,000 cents.
But plusses also dotted the board on Monday, among them multi-industrial group TZI up 10 cents to 1,010, Caps which added 20 cents to 1,700 and NMB which put on 50 to 3,350 cents.
"Volumes are still low indicating the sellers are small investors and I see corporate results coming in the next couple of weeks lifting the index," one market analyst told Reuters.
There was little change on the secondary mining index on Monday although brokers reported more activity in some of the gold counters after a firming of international bullion prices.
However gold counters Falgold and Ashanti lost five and 1,500 cents respectively to 60 and 9,000. The only climber was coal miner Wankie, up five cents to 520.
The index shed 14.12 or 1.41 percent to close at 988.41,
